Transform random effects and their covariance matrices back

Source: R/scaling.R
rescale_ranefs.Rd

In JAGS, the random effects b of a grouping level enter the linear predictor as sum_j b_j * (z_j - c_j) / s_j, with z_1 = 1 (random intercept) and the random-slope variables z_j, each centred and scaled separately. Written as a function of the original z, this gives the random effects on the original scale:

Usage

rescale_ranefs(rescaled, MCMC, coefs, scale_pars, info_list, data_list, groups)

Arguments

rescaled

MCMC sample (matrix) in which the coefficients are already transformed back (rescale_coefs()).

MCMC

MCMC sample of one chain on the scale used in JAGS (mcmc object or matrix).

coefs

data.frame with one row per regression coefficient (do.call(rbind, get_coef_names(info_list))); used to find the coefficients in the means of the random effects.

scale_pars

data.frame of scaling parameters (columns center and scale, one row per design-matrix column, named by the column), with centre 0 and scale 1 for columns that are not scaled.

info_list

list with the model information of each sub-model (get_model_info()).

data_list

data list passed to JAGS (for the names of design-matrix columns).

groups

list of grouping information (Mlist$groups; for the number of groups per level, and to find the rows of covariates per group).

Value

rescaled, with the random effects and their covariance matrices transformed back.

Details

b = A b_s + delta,     D = A D_s A'

  • A undoes the scaling of the random slopes; the centring is constant within a group and moves to the random intercept (ranef_transformation()).

  • delta: with hierarchical centring, the means of the random effects contain fixed effects. These are transformed back separately (rescale_coefs(), e.g. the intercept takes the centring of all covariates); delta keeps b consistent with them (ranef_shift()).

A does not need the data, so the random effects are transformed back also when a random-slope variable has missing values. delta usually does not need the data either. If it depends on covariates (see ranef_covariate_shift()), the values of each group are used: observed or, if missing, imputed values (if they were monitored). Without them, the random effects of that group are set to NA, with a warning.

The random effects are transformed per "block": the random effects that share one covariance matrix (get_ranef_blocks()). Usually, a block holds the random effects of one outcome at one grouping level; with rd_vcov = "full", it holds those of several outcomes, and A then has one submatrix on the diagonal per outcome (zero elsewhere).
